correctness.rationale: PASS. For d>=3 and 0<=t<1, the affine plane through te_d is sampled by a Haar normal U=G/||G||. Orient U_d>0. The dth coordinate pair straddles the plane and among i<d exactly M_t-1 more coordinate pairs straddle it; the remaining d-M_t pairs have both vertices on its negative side. Every generic k-section face crosses one (k+1)-face of the crosspolytope. Counting signed choices by j=k+2 yields H_{d,m}(z)=(1+2z)^d-(1+z)^m-(1+z)^m(1+2z)^{d-m}+1 with the constant adjusted for the twice-subtracted empty face. Conditioning on |G_d| gives independent comparison indicators and precisely the stated half-normal binomial-mixture integral. As t approaches 1 from below, exchangeable absolute Gaussian order statistics make m uniform on {1,...,d}, but the section at t=1 is not covered. Difference H_{d,m+1}-H_{d,m}=z(1+z)^m((1+2z)^{d-m-1}-1) establishes componentwise monotonicity and the final tie m=d-1,d. Recomputed coefficients/number of distinct vectors and rank-uniform vertex means/variances exactly for d=3,...,10; the mean 2(d²-1)/3 and variance (d-2)(d-1)(d+1)(4d-7)/45 agree. For d=3 the small Gaussian cone gives the stated 2/pi arctan(t²/sqrt(1+2t²)) quadrilateral probability. The all-d proof comes from sign counting and Gaussian exchangeability, not the finite tests.
